description:
Why Is a Day on Venus Longer Than Its Year?

Venus spins so slowly, and backwards, that one rotation takes longer than one trip around the Sun. On Venus the Sun rises in the west.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

#venus #planets #space #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Imagine a world where your birthday comes around before the day ends.
That's Venus. It takes two hundred and twenty-five Earth days to go around the Sun.
But it takes two hundred and forty-three days to spin around just once.
So one turn of Venus is longer than its whole year.
segments.headline: A day longer than a year

segments.text: And it spins backwards. If you stood on Venus, the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.
segments.headline: The Sun rises in the west

segments.text: Because it spins backwards, sunrise to sunrise takes about a hundred and seventeen Earth days.
